subject: docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-098.draft.md
summary: D-098 materially improves the contested D-094 contract: the hosted labels are honestly fleet classes; the four public-runner resource rows match GitHub's current official table; N=21 plus nearest-rank gives distinct p95 and p99 order statistics; help and version are separate series; host, executable, and process architectures must match; Rosetta is forbidden on both macOS classes; all D-006 numeric threshold numerals remain unchanged; and the 18-of-18 arithmetic and no-QUALIFIED/no-SATISFIED/no-implementation boundaries are correct. The contract still cannot support G03/G04 naming. First, weekly image changes force an absolute-only rebaseline, silently disabling D-006's operative second-release 10% regression rule precisely when the substrate normally rolls. Second, the sample unit and cache schedule do not define reproducible command-by-binary cold/warm pairs or how G04 baseline/peak RSS series aggregate against D-006 thresholds and regression. The preflight also still omits deterministic architecture/image/brand/OS observables and maps the documented 14 GB storage row to an unjustified root-filesystem-size test. G03/G04 must remain reserved and condition 4 must remain 16 of 18 and PARTLY MET.

objections.title: Weekly image rebaseline silently disables D-006's second-release regression rule
objections.finding: D-006's operative rule says every qualified clause-1-through-4 measurement from the second qualified release onward may not regress more than 10% against the previous qualified release without the full waiver. D-098 says that rule and its numeral stand, but lines 103-110 apply it only when image identity and CPU brand are the same, declare different identity/brand an absolute-only rebaseline, and expressly say weekly image rolls force rebaseline. Because the proposed paired design reruns the previous and candidate binaries on each current VM, a historical image difference need not confound the comparison; both binaries can be compared contemporaneously on the same accepted substrate. The automatic rebaseline therefore evades rather than repairs the regression obligation. The phrase 'same image identity and same CPU brand' is also scope-ambiguous: it does not say whether sameness is required within each pair, across all 21 jobs, or against the prior qualification cohort.
evidence: Adopted D-006 states that the first qualified release is the sole base case and the regress-only rule activates from the second qualified release onward; a waiver requires product and release authority, expiry, a measured residual, and no waiver of inherited semantic/trust blockers.
D-098 lines 38-40 claim the 10% rule stands, while lines 103-110 create repeated rebaseline base cases and say the rule does not span them.

D-098 itself recognizes weekly image rolls. GitHub's official runner-images source is continuously updated, so image identity commonly changes independently of an OpenSIP release: https://github.com/actions/runner-images .
The contemporaneous paired execution in D-098 lines 103-106 already provides the mechanism needed to control the current VM/image for both binaries; no unpaired historical distribution is required.
objections.impact: A candidate may regress more than 10% relative to the previous qualified release yet pass whenever the hosted image has rolled, provided it remains under the looser absolute thresholds. That changes the substantive D-006 base-case/waiver regime while claiming only an exact-machine/exact-OS successor and makes the 10% protection likely dormant for ordinary release cadences.
objections.requiredRepair: Choose and state one honest rule. Preferred: on every second-or-later release, run the digest-pinned previous qualified binary and candidate as a recorded, counterbalanced pair on every accepted current VM; define the exact paired aggregate for each D-006 metric; and apply the 10% rule even when the historical qualification used another image. Define whether image/brand cohorts must be homogeneous or may be mixed as paired strata. If a previous binary truly cannot run on the current class, require a separately reviewed successor or D-006's full waiver rather than an automatic rebaseline. Alternatively, explicitly widen D-098's preference-laden successor scope to replace D-006's base-case and regression activation rule, record the protection lost and warrant, and stop claiming that the rule stands unchanged. Refreeze after repair.

objections.title: The sample/cache/RSS matrix is not reproducibly defined
objections.finding: The contract defines N and order-statistic ranks for a scalar series, but it never defines the complete sample matrix or execution order that supplies those series. One job is said to yield separate help and version samples, later releases add previous and candidate binaries, and every series has cold and warm states. The cold rule performs a purge and requires a first execution, yet only one command/binary can be first after a single purge; the warm rule says 'immediately after one completed cold pair, same binary' without identifying whether the pair is the two commands or the two releases, which binary is warmed, or whether another binary/command may intervene. No reset, block, counterbalancing, or order-recording rule resolves this. G04 is even less defined: 'the D-006 lifecycle commands' covers help, version, and doctor-read-only, each producing steady-baseline and peak RSS quantities, but the subject does not define those command-by-metric series, whether cold/warm applies to each, which aggregate must satisfy the 40/50/60/100 MB numerals, or how the 10% rule applies to them. 'Paired per-percentile results' supplies no formula and does not map the non-percentile D-006 RSS thresholds.
evidence: D-098 lines 67-74 define help/version series and N=21 ranks; lines 103-106 add two binaries per VM; lines 112-117 define only one purge/first-exec narrative and an ambiguous completed cold pair.

Adopted D-006 separately bounds help/version steady baseline and peak RSS and doctor-read-only steady baseline and peak RSS, and applies its regression rule to qualified clause-1-through-4 measurements.

The G04 row in file 08 requires raw RSS traces and methodology. D-098 names the identifier and flips condition 4 to MET while leaving the fleet-level methodology capable of multiple incompatible implementations.
objections.impact: Two conforming harness authors can produce different cold/warm samples, different order effects, and different G04 pass/fail outcomes from the same 21 VMs. A contract that cannot unambiguously generate or evaluate both G03 and G04 measurements is not the complete hosted-fleet successor needed to convert their reservations into named identifiers.
objections.requiredRepair: Specify the exact accepted-pair matrix and per-VM sequence. At minimum enumerate platform × command × metric × state × release-binary series; state when cache purge/reset occurs so every cold observation is genuinely first after its own reset; make each warm observation immediately follow the matching cold observation without an intervening command/binary; counterbalance and record previous/candidate order; and require 21 accepted matched pairs for each governed series. For G04, enumerate help, version, and doctor-read-only steady/peak RSS series, select an explicit fleet aggregate or all-samples rule for each absolute numeral, and define the paired 10% formula without pooling commands or metrics. Preserve the deliberate analyze and consented-probe exclusions. Refreeze after repair.

objections.title: The fail-closed preflight still lacks deterministic observables
objections.finding: D-098 accepts ADV-D094-T3-03 and now names the host, executable, and process architecture categories, but it does not name commands/fields for any of those three, the CPU-brand stratum, image identity, OS family, or the translation query. It also defines the class using the documented public-repository row but does not verify repository visibility. The storage rule equates GitHub's documented '14 GB Storage (SSD)' value with root filesystem total size in [10,20] GB via `df -k /`; the official table does not define that column as the guest root filesystem's total-block field, and the draft does not specify which `df` field or whether configured capacity, free bytes, or available bytes is intended. RAM has a byte conversion and tolerance, but storage has neither a justified unit conversion nor a source-to-observable mapping.
evidence: D-098 lines 76-92 name required facts but supply commands only for CPU count, RAM, and `df`; even the `df` output field is not identified.

GitHub's official hosted-runner table supports the selected labels and CPU/RAM/storage/architecture values but presents a service resource row, not a guest-observation algorithm: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners .
The prior ADV-D094-T3-03 repair expressly required commands/fields, units, and configured-versus-available semantics, not category names alone.
objections.impact: Independent harness implementations may disagree on admitting the same VM, and the literal storage test may reject the documented fleet or validate a different property. This weakens the fail-closed claim and auditability even though the intended class and anti-translation policy are clear.
objections.requiredRepair: For every platform, define the exact command/API and normalized field for host, executable, and process architecture; CPU brand; image identity; OS family; and translation status. Verify public-repository context or make its resource-row properties independently fail closed. Define storage as a specific configured/free/available byte quantity on a named mount, identify the `df` field and unit conversion, and justify its tolerance against the official row. State cohort handling for brand/image mismatches.
